plugins.name: Bloodsand
plugins.description: A client-only, cosmetic gore mod: worms spray blood when hit, wear it on their skin, open layered wounds, get black eyes, throw up blood, spill intestines, spurt from their arteries and leave trails and pools. Deaths and big hits throw meat, bone and organs. Droplets leave splats and drying pools; heavy hits spatter the lens. Only reads game state and draws. No effect on the simulation.

versions.changelog:
- Gore on Sunstone's human skin: with Sunstone 2.2's Worm skin on a tone, blood, gashes, black eyes, burns and the torn
  belly are painted on the new skin (found by the mark Sunstone leaves in the scene instead of by the game's peach colour,
  which a human tone no longer has), and wounds and blood are lit by that worm's skin brightness, so they look as raw on a
  dark skin as on the peach. Pooled blood keeps its red on a dark skin instead of turning black.
- Black eyes on a human skin are a real bruise: the skin's own colour gone purple-red and dark (plum on a fair skin, a
  deep brown on a dark one), softer than the cartoon's near-black mask, which the game's peach keeps.
- With Sunstone 2.2 the game's peach is found by Sunstone's mark as well as by its colour, so wounds also show under
  Lunar's purple light and on a poisoned worm. The colour test always counts too, so should Sunstone's shader not run the
  peach is still found (a moustache drawn as real hair can then catch a wound where its highlights have the skin's
  colour). On a dark tone a thin smear of blood is red over the brown, with a stronger wet sheen, and no longer washes
  the skin under it pale.
- With Sunstone 2.2, a worm seen through a ledge (the game shows the worm whose turn it is through what stands in front of
  it) keeps its wounds and blood there too, a little fainter, instead of having them cut off in a hard line at the
  ledge's edge.
  Nothing changes without Sunstone 2.2.

Runs on Melange 0.7 and every later version: the plugin no longer names an upper Melange version, so a new
Melange release no longer moves it to `Mods\.incompatible`. No other change.

Gorier again: worms spurt blood, leave trails and pools, and come apart. Gibs: deaths and very big hits throw ray-marched chunks of meat, bone shards and organs that bounce, slide and stay (new Gibs setting). Pools and trails: wounded worms drip and badly hurt ones leave a smear, dying worms grow a pool and the gravestone sits in it (new Pools & trails setting). Arterial spurts from the wounds of worms below about a third of their health. Also includes 1.2: ray-marched intestines, a spray for each weapon, droplets that splat on walls and ground, glossy sprite droplets, a lens splatter that refracts, skin-only blood and a readable black eye. Uses Melange 0.6 (landRay, sprites) when present and falls back on older versions.
Runs on Melange 0.5. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.4. No other change.

Fixes blood, wounds, black eyes and ground stains not being drawn at all on some machines: the shader that paints the
worms was large enough that a graphics driver could accept it and then draw nothing with it, which also discarded the
stains drawn before it. It now picks the one worm a pixel belongs to and does the long work once. Much more blood from
ordinary hits: more and larger droplets, longer bleeding, larger and darker stains, and a first hit now leaves a worm
clearly bloodied instead of speckled. Black eyes no longer fade out while a worm walks.

Badly hurt worms now show it in three more ways. Their eyes blacken as health falls: one eye first, then both. Worms
at a quarter of their health or less occasionally throw up blood. Some worms, picked at random each match, have their
intestines out once they are badly wounded: coils in a torn belly and a loop hanging from it that swings as the worm
moves. Blood, wounds and the new marks now turn with the way a worm faces, not the way it last walked. Needs Melange
0.3.5 or later, which gives plugins a worm's facing angle (`yaw` in `wum.game.worms()`). New settings: Worms throw up
blood and Intestines; black eyes follow Blood on worms.

First release. Worms throw blood the moment they are hurt, away from the explosion and sized by the damage, bleed for
a while afterwards and burst when they die. Hit worms wear blood on their skin that stays with them as they move, and
worms low on health open gaping wounds: up to five gashes with torn edges and running blood, which close again if the
worm is healed. Blood stains the ground in a depth-projected Post-FX pass that follows the terrain, and heavy hits
spatter the camera lens. Client-only and cosmetic: it reads worm health and positions and the game's damage and
explosion messages, and only draws. Needs Melange 0.3.4 or later for `wum.postfx.setTransient`, which lets it feed the
Post-FX passes every frame without anything being written to `Melange.ini`. Settings: Blood (Off / Light / Heavy /
Absurd), Blood on worms, Blood on the ground, Splatter on the lens and Blood colour (Red / Green).

plugins.name: Caravan
plugins.description: Imports the maps of Renewation HD 0.2A2 into Melange on your PC, from mod.worms.pro or a zip you already have. Contains no maps itself.

versions.changelog:
Runs on Melange 0.7 and every later version: the plugin no longer names an upper Melange version, so a new
Melange release no longer moves it to `Mods\.incompatible`. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.6. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.5. No other change.

First release: a recipe for Melange's local content importer that brings the 174 importable maps of Renewation HD
0.2A2 into your own game folder. Downloads the official zip from mod.worms.pro (or uses a copy you already have),
verifies its SHA-256, and generates map packs on your PC. Caravan itself contains no maps.

plugins.name: Kanly
plugins.description: Adds the Kanly game style (five-minute rounds, then fast-rising water, weapons that unlock as the match goes on) and Kanly Melee (the same timings, melee weapons, grenades and utilities only), four Kanly Weapon Factory presets and Kanly sudden-death music. Also fixes controls (camera and aim invert, mouse sensitivity) and shows control hints and a legend. Client-side.

versions.changelog:
Weapons now unlock as the match progresses and run out after a few uses, in both styles.

- Kanly: weapons have an unlock turn (Delay) in four tiers, start, turn 1, turn 2 and turn 3. The match opens with basics
  and utilities; mid-tier weapons come at turn 1, heavy ones at turn 2, and the super weapons (Concrete Donkey, Super
  Airstrike, Fatkins, Starburst, Flood, Alien Abduction, Weapon Factory weapon) at turn 3.
- Ammo is cut hard: basics 3 to 4, utilities 2 to 3, mid tier 2 (power-ups 1), heavy and super weapons 1. Nothing is
  unlimited and crates stay on.
- The 15 mystery crate entries now get 1 ammo and unlock at turn 1.
- Kanly Melee: the same tiers for the allowed weapons (no super tier), same bans.
- Netplay: the host and every peer need Kanly 1.3.0.

Adds a second game style, Kanly Melee.

- Kanly Melee: the Kanly timings (five minute round, then fast-rising water) with close-range weapons only. Bazooka,
  Homing Missile, Shotgun, Sniper Rifle, Poison Arrow, Sentry Gun, No More Nails, Bubble Trouble, Starburst, Super
  Sheep, Weapon Factory weapon, both airstrikes, Concrete Donkey, Fatkins, Alien Abduction, Scouser, Flood and Crate
  Shower are removed from the loadout and from crates. Fire Punch and Prod get 5 uses each (2 in Kanly).
- Fix to the docs: Kanly's 15 mystery crate entries get 10 ammo and no delay, they are not left as in Standard.
- Netplay: the host and every peer need Kanly 1.2.0, because the game style list positions shift with the new style.

Adds control fixes and control hints. Needs Melange 0.8.0 or later.

- Camera and aim: choose the 3rd-person camera Y direction (game, standard or inverted; standard is the new default),
  the first-person aim Y direction, whether the camera invert also applies in Blimp view, and a camera and an aim
  mouse sensitivity.
- Control hints: short, faded key and mouse prompts at the bottom centre on your own turn (off, learning or always).
  In learning mode a prompt disappears after you have used it three times.
- Controls legend: press F1 (or Ctrl+H, a setting) during a match for the full control list.
- A one-time note on the first match about the camera Y default.

Runs on Melange 0.7 and every later version: the plugin no longer names an upper Melange version, so a new
Melange release no longer moves it to `Mods\.incompatible`. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.6. No other change.

First release. Adds the Kanly game style and four Weapon Factory presets (Kanly Red, Blue, Green and Yellow) to the
vanilla menus, and replaces the sudden-death music with four Kanly tracks. Needs Melange 0.5.0 or later.

plugins.name: Kindjal
plugins.description: Every weapon shifted a dimension darker: melee that maims, explosives that hit harder and throw worms a little further than vanilla, three new weapons (Acid Spitter, Acid Flask, Crucible) whose acid smokes and clings to a worm's skin, new names, new sounds. Content mod: every player in an online match needs it.

versions.changelog:
- The acid eats Sunstone's human skin: with Sunstone 2.2's Worm skin on a tone, the acid finds the skin by the mark
  Sunstone leaves in the scene instead of by the game's peach colour (which a human tone no longer has), and lights itself
  by that worm's skin brightness, so it looks the same on a dark skin as on the peach. It still leaves blood, wounds and
  guts alone. With Sunstone 2.2 the game's peach is found by the mark too, so the acid also shows under Lunar's purple
  light. The colour test always counts too, so should Sunstone's shader not run the peach is still found. On a dark tone
  the acid covers more of the skin under it, so it reads as the poison's green, not a faint olive stain. Nothing changes
  without Sunstone 2.2.
- With Sunstone 2.2, the acid also shows on a worm seen through a ledge (the game shows the worm whose turn it is through
  what stands in front of it), a little fainter, instead of stopping in a hard line at the ledge's edge.
- The preview event (`mod.kindjal.preview`, `what = "acid"`) takes `target = "active"` to coat the active worm.

- Knockback brought back to near the game's own: every weapon now throws worms about 1.2 times as hard as vanilla, over
  about 1.1 times the reach, instead of two to three times as hard (the Ripper 0.64 to 0.35, the Gorger 1.80 to 0.72,
  the Earthquake Ass 1.30 to 0.56, the Crucible 1.35 to 0.62). Damage, blast radius and craters are unchanged.
- The Railspike, Knifeman and Rust Canister, which have no knockback in the game, get a small one.
- Knockback is tunable: `KNOCKBACK`, `REACH` and `MELEE` at the top of `mod/sim/main.lua` scale every knockback and
  reach, the three new weapons included. They live in the sim script, not on the Mods page, because the match cannot
  read Mods-page settings; the file is content-hashed, so every online player must have the same values.
- Two optional add-on plugins pick a different knockback power: Kindjal Heavy (about 1.7 times vanilla) and Kindjal
  Brutal (the 1.0.0 numbers). Enable one; every online player must enable the same one.
- Weapon descriptions no longer promise worms thrown across the map.

First release. Needs Melange 0.9.0 or later.

- Every vanilla weapon re-statted darker at match start (damage, blast radius, crater, knockback) and renamed: Nail
  Bat, Hellfist, Shiv, Railspike, Ripper, Pipe Bomb, Blast Keg, Profane Grenade, Plantain Hell, Nail Cluster, Bear Trap,
  Harpoon, Carpet Bombing, Carrion Drop, Earthquake Ass, Rabid Flock, Plague Ram, Hangwoman, Knifeman, Gorger, Dead
  Star, Slug Gun, Elephant Gun, Gibbet Turret, Plague Arrow, Rust Canister.
- Three new weapons: Acid Spitter, Acid Flask and Crucible, with their own icons and models; every renamed weapon
  gets its own panel and HUD icon.
- Models: every renamed weapon has its own held and/or projectile model (37 mesh banks), and the Airstrike and Super
  Airstrike helicopters are replaced by a black and a bone-white gunship. 19 banks are static meshes built from
  scratch; 18 are clones of vanilla skinned meshes that keep the game's rig, skin weights, animation clips and UV layout
  (see "What is derived from the game" in the README). Seen in play so far: the Nail Bat, Acid Flask and Crucible in hand.
- Acid that clings to a worm's skin, bubbles and smokes; acid puddles; melee impact sparks and hit-flash; new sounds.
- Content mod: every player in an online match needs the same version.

plugins.name: Kindjal Brutal
plugins.description: Kindjal add-on: brings back Kindjal 1.0.0's original knockback, two to three times vanilla (Ripper 0.64, Gorger 1.80, Earthquake Ass 1.30). Enable at most one Kindjal knockback preset. Content mod: every player in an online match needs it.

versions.changelog: First release. Needs Melange 0.9.0 or later and Kindjal 1.1.0 or later.

plugins.name: Kindjal Heavy
plugins.description: Kindjal add-on: throws worms harder. Multiplies the knockback Kindjal sets by 1.4 and its reach by 1.15, about 1.7 times vanilla knockback. Enable at most one Kindjal knockback preset. Content mod: every player in an online match needs it.

versions.changelog: First release. Needs Melange 0.9.0 or later and Kindjal 1.1.0 or later.

plugins.name: Sunstone
plugins.description: A dramatic, client-only graphics overhaul: sharper textures, anti-aliasing and sharpening, grading, atmosphere (SSAO, aerial perspective, bloom), soft shadows, per-pixel lighting and water. No effect on the simulation.

versions.changelog:
- **Worm skin is rebuilt in the model shader.** The skin and hair used to be found by colour in the finished frame; now
  Sunstone's lit-model shader knows exactly which texels are skin before any light or grade. No more peach patches on
  tails and faces, no camouflage blotches, and moustaches, hats, glasses and eyes always keep their colours. Gloved
  hands that show bare skin take the tone too.
- **Fast and reliable:** nothing measurable at the game's camera, about 0.1 to 0.4 ms at Ultra with a worm close up
  (was 0.3 to 1.1 ms), and no stall when you change Worm skin or Worm hair.
- **Clearly distinct tones, fully covered.** Light, Tan and Brown can be picked as well as Fair, Medium, Olive, Deep and
  Mixed. Each tone has its own undertone (pink ivory, golden beige, warm tan, muted olive, golden and red browns), and
  dark tones keep warm mid-tones in shade instead of going black.
- **Skin you can see from the game's own distance:** blotches of blood and pigment, folds and wrinkles round the neck
  and down the back, a fine grain that catches the light, moles, blemishes and freckles, an oily T-zone that shines
  against matte cheeks, darker skin around the eyes, and pores up close; soft warm light under and through the skin, natural eye whites, fair skin that keeps its colour in the sun, less colour banding, and a little
  variation from worm to worm.
- **Hair:** moustaches, and with Realistic hair hats the afro, pigtails and crests, are found by their texture and drawn
  with strands and a hair fibre's highlights.
- **Bloodsand 1.4.0 and Kindjal 1.2.0** paint on the new skin (the skin marks itself for them); older versions only
  paint on the game's peach, and Sunstone says so on screen.

- New **Worm skin** setting (Game / Fair / Medium / Olive / Deep / Mixed, default Game): re-renders the worms' cartoon
  peach as near photo-real human skin, with subsurface scattering, a sheen that varies over the body, pores, fine skin
  lines and folds lit by the sun, blotches, freckles, flush and faint veins. Detail follows each pixel's footprint, so it
  never shimmers, and moves with the worm. Mixed gives every worm its own tone from its name.
- New **Worm hair** setting (Game / Natural / Mixed, default Game): moustaches become real-looking hair, with strands,
  darker roots, the two highlights of a hair fibre and a ragged edge. Natural keeps each moustache's colour family;
  Mixed picks a natural colour per worm.
- **Realistic hair hats too** (experimental, off by default): dark wigs and afros get a hair texture. Found by colour,
  place and texture, so a brown wig in the cowboy hat's hue is left alone; a hat is never recoloured. See the README.
- Works with Bloodsand and Kindjal unchanged: the effect runs after them (orders 51 to 54) and recolours only what is
  still skin, so blood, wounds, guts and acid keep their colours with no peach rim, and a black eye becomes a real
  bruise on the new tone. Eyes, hats and the sand are untouched; lips keep their pink and the tongue, teeth and inside
  of the mouth are left as drawn.
- Worms standing close together are fully re-rendered.
- No cost with both settings on Game; otherwise it runs only in a match (not yet measured in game).

Runs on Melange 0.7 and every later version: the plugin no longer names an upper Melange version, so a new
Melange release no longer moves it to `Mods\.incompatible`. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.6. No other change.
Runs on Melange 0.5. No other change.

- Natural grass and foliage: meadows and leaves move from neon toward real greens, while gas, barrels, water and sky
  keep their colours. Set per theme, and off on Arctic, Lunar and Horror.
- New light: a stronger sun, deep soft cast shadows without stripes on steep or grazing ground, worms and props
  grounded by darker undersides and short contact shadows, and a warm sun with cooler shade where the theme suits it.
- Atmosphere: haze that gives distant islands depth, a soft sun glow, drifting cloud shadows and, on Bold, light
  shafts. Each is held back where it does not fit: no sun glow or shafts on Horror, Lunar and War.
- Water: clear shallows that show the floor in the sea's own hue, caustics, reflections of the scenery with no seams
  beside cliffs, calmer glints with no pale bands far out, and lighter shore foam without bright outlines.
- Light and grade now work in linear light, with a new display transform that rolls bright colours softly to white,
  bloom and a dither against banding. This replaces the separate grade, fog, sky glow and bloom effects of 1.7,
  which are switched off on upgrade.
- Ambient occlusion is horizon-based and applied in linear light.
- Bold adds distance blur on far scenery, fine film grain and a lens finish (dirt, flare, colour fringes). New
  Distance blur, Film grain and Lens effects settings turn them off.
- Every theme keeps its character: Horror its olive sea, Arctic its white snow, Lunar its violet shade, Building its
  grey stone, and bright sand stays below white.
- Low uses a single-pass version of the new colour, and Low and Subtle are no darker than Off. Ultra runs the heavier
  effects at half scale on the supersampled scene.
- Measured at 1920x1080 on a mid-range desktop GPU, paused frame: Bold adds about 1.5 ms of frame GPU time over Off,
  Ultra about 6.9 ms.
- Runs on Melange 0.4. No other change.
- Fixes the sea turning pale and losing its shallows and shore foam in a match once the camera moved.

- Bold water keeps the hue of the game's own sea on every theme, only deeper and more saturated: Horror's olive
  sea no longer turns green, and Pirate's pale cyan stays cyan rather than drifting blue.
- Aerial perspective hazes the sea and other level surfaces in their own hue, so a tinted sky no longer shifts it.
- A new opt-in **Ultra** quality: Bold with 2x2 supersampling, the scene rendered at twice the resolution each way and
  scaled down. SMAA is off there, since supersampling already smooths those edges. Measured at 1920x1080 on a
  mid-range desktop GPU, paused frame: about 7.5 ms of frame GPU time (Bold 3.9 ms) and about 350 MB more video
  memory. Needs a Melange with `wum.graphics.setSupersample`; an older one renders Ultra as Bold.
- Blurs, sharpening, bloom, the grade's local contrast and the texture-relief and ripple fades scale with
  Melange's render scale, so they look the same with supersampling.

- Bold water is a deep, saturated version of the game's own sea colour: a calmer reflection, no teal cast, and
  crisp white glints that cover the water below them instead of turning cream over sandy shallows.
- The grade no longer turns bright blue teal: a cool colour that leaves the range is scaled back instead of having
  its blue channel clipped.
- Sharpening and local contrast fade out on surfaces right in front of the camera, and sharpening leaves faint
  steps alone, so magnified textures no longer turn blocky.
- Measured at 1920x1080 on a mid-range desktop GPU, paused frame, Off and Bold alternated: Bold adds about 0.08 ms of
  render-thread CPU time with Melange's cheaper GLSL parameter feed (0.14 ms before).
